questions.question: If 60 litres of a milk solution has 40% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make the milk 60% in the solution?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial volume = 60 liters

Initial milk % = 40%

Desired milk % = 60%

**Formula:**

(Initial quantity of milk + Milk added) / (Initial total volume + Milk added) = Desired milk %

**Calculation:**

Initial quantity of milk: 60 × 40% = 24 liters

Let x = Milk to be added.

(24 + x) / (60 + x) = 60%

⇒ 24 + x = 0.6 × (60 + x)

⇒ 24 + x = 36 + 0.6x

⇒ x - 0.6x = 36 - 24

⇒ 0.4x = 12

⇒ x = 12/0.4

⇒ x = 30 liters

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: In two circles centred at O and O’, the distance between the centres of both circles is 17 cm. The points of contact of a direct common tangent between the circles are P and Q. If the radii of both circles are 7 cm and 15 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

The Radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 15 cm

The distance between their centres is 17 cm.

Formula used:

Length of direct common tangent = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} 

Where D = Distance between their centers, r1 = radius of the bigger circle and r2 = radius of the smaller circle

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/726975bbefbb6bc401e04d6b4c972ebcce6acec738379596570646b2b5bc2185.png] 

According to the formula,

Length of PQ = sqrt {17² - (15 - 7)²}

⇒ Length of PQ = sqrt {289 - 64}

⇒ Length of PQ = 15 cm

∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 15 cm.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 15% on an article and still makes a profit of 20%. What does the shopkeeper pay for an article whose marked price is ₹7,200?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 15%

Marked Price (MP) = ₹7,200

Profit = 20%

**Formula used:**

Sale Price (SP) after discount = MP - (Discount% × MP)

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit %)

**Solution:**

SP = 7200 - (0.15 × 7200) = 7200 - 1080 = ₹6,120

CP = 6120 / (1 + 0.20) = 6120 / 1.20 = ₹5,100

**The shopkeeper pays ₹5,100 for the article.**

questions.question: Find the area of a rhombus if the perimeter of the rhombus is 52 cm, and one of its diagonals is 10 cm long.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side** of the **rhombus** (a) = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

One **half-diagonal** = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13), the other **half-diagonal** is 12 cm.

**Full second diagonal** (d₂) = 12 × 2 = 24 cm.

**Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = (1/2) × 10 × 24 = 120 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of **rhombus** = 52 cm

One **diagonal** (d₁) = 10 cm

**Formula used:**

1) **Perimeter** = 4 × side (a)

2) **Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

3) a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a1a654d398b899e59e55d4ecc5f8eaee53219713c42bddce8ac771fe7fc0f51.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Side** (a) = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm

⇒ (d₂/2)² = a² − (d₁/2)²

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 13² − (10/2)²

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 169 − 25 = 144

⇒ d₂/2 = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ **Second diagonal** (d₂) = 12 × 2 = 24 cm

⇒ **Area** = (1/2) × 10 × 24

⇒ **Area** = 5 × 24 = 120 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All **four sides** are equal and **diagonals** bisect each other at **90°**.

Area using Base and Height

Area = **Base × Height**. This formula is used when the altitude and side length are known.

Diagonal and Side Relation

The sum of **squares of diagonals** is equal to 4 × (square of side): d₁² + d₂² = 4a².</p

A speedboat, whose speed in 20 km/h in still water, goes 35 km downstream and comes back in a total of 8 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the speedboat in still water = 20 km/h

Distance downstream = 35 km

Total time for the round trip = 8 hours

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the stream be (v) km/h.

Downstream Speed= (20 + v) km/h

Upstream Speed = (20 - v) km/h

Time for downstream = (35/(20 + v))

Time for upstream = (35/(20 - v))

Total Time = Time downstream + Time upstream

⇒ (35 / (20 + v) + 35 / (20 - v) = 8) hours

⇒ 35 / (20 + v) + 35 / (20 - v) = 8

⇒ 35(20 - v) + 35(20 + v) = 8(20² - v²)

⇒ 700 - 35v + 700 + 35v = 8(400 - v2)

⇒ 1400 = 3200 - 8v2

⇒ 8v2 = 3200 - 1400

 ⇒8v2 = 1800

⇒ v2 = 225

⇒ v = 15

**Therefore, the speed of the stream is 15 km/h.**

questions.question: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio: 4 Men = 6 Boys ⇒ 2 Men = 3 Boys.

Convert Men into Boys: 6 Men = (3 ÷ 2) × 6 = 9 Boys.

Total Group Requirement: 6 Men + 11 Boys = 9 Boys + 11 Boys = 20 Boys.

Using M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ ⇒ 6 Boys × 20 Days = 20 Boys × Days.

Required Days = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 4 Men = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Man = 4 × 20 = 80 days.

Time taken by 6 Boys = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Boy = 6 × 20 = 120 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual days; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days.

 
 

 **Person**

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of 6 Men = 6 × 3 = 18 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of 11 Boys = 11 × 2 = 22 units/day.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (6 Men + 11 Boys) = 18 + 22 = 40 units/day.

⇒ Required Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Required Time = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Formula

The relationship between men, days, and hours is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ Time).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the product of efficiency and time.</p

questions.question: In an election between P and Q, P gets 40% of the total votes and thus loses by 10 votes. The total number of votes is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P gets 40% of the total votes

P loses by 10 votes

**Calculation:**

Total votes = 100x

Votes for P = 40% of (100x)

Votes for Q = 100x - Votes for P

P loses by 10 votes, which means:

Votes for Q = Votes for P + 10

Since P gets 40% of the total votes, we have:

Votes for P = 40x

Therefore, the votes for Q can be expressed as:

Votes for Q = (40x + 10)

According to the question,

⇒ 100x = 40x + 40x + 10

⇒ 100x = 80x + 10

⇒ 20x = 10

⇒ x = 1/2

Total votes = (100 × 1/2) = 50

**Therefore, the total number of votes is 50.**

questions.question: If tan A = (2)/(5) find the value of (sec ² A)/(operatorname{cosec)² A}.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that **tan A = sin A / cos A** and **sec A = 1 / cos A**, **cosec A = 1 / sin A**.

The expression **sec² A / cosec² A** simplifies to **(1 / cos² A) / (1 / sin² A) = sin² A / cos² A = tan² A**.

Given **tan A = 2/5**.

∴ **tan² A = (2/5)² = 4/25**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51f327a6fce67a6ee2230ebe76b5fc91e034c897f2798d31f18c0c5474ec0302.png] 

**Given:** tan A = 2/5

**Formula Used:** sec² A = 1 + tan² A; cosec² A = 1 + cot² A; cot A = 1/tan A

⇒ Expression = sec² A / cosec² A

⇒ Expression = (1/cos² A) ÷ (1/sin² A)

⇒ Expression = sin² A / cos² A = tan² A

⇒ Value = (2/5)²

⇒ Value = 4/25

**∴ The correct answer is 4/25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ; cosec θ = 1/sin θ; cot θ = 1/tan θ.</p

questions.question: The LCM of two prime numbers x and y (x > y) is 533. The value of 4y - x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

LCM(x, y) = 533

x and y are prime numbers

x > y

**Formula:**

LCM(x, y) = x × y (since x and y are primes)

**Calculation:**

Solving: 533 = x × y

Prime factorization of 533:

533 = 13 × 41

So, x = 41 and y = 13 (x > y)

Finding 4y - x:

4y - x = 4(13) - 41

= 52 - 41

= 11

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is doubled, then its surface area will be increased by:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius = r

**Formula:**

Surface Area = 4πr²

**Calculation:**

Original Surface Area: 4πr²

Doubling radius: New radius = 2r

⇒ New Surface Area = 4π(2r)² = 16πr²

⇒ Increase in Surface Area: 16πr2 - 4πr2 = 12πr2

⇒ Percentage = 12πr²/4πr² × 100 = 300%

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

**Solution:**

⇒ CI = 25000(1 + 12/100)³ - 25000

⇒ 25000(1.12)³ - 25000

⇒ 25000 × 1.404928 - 25000

⇒ 35123.2 - 25000 = ₹10,123.20

**The compound interest is ₹10,123.20.**

questions.question: A solid sphere made of wax of radius 12 cm is melted and cast into solid hemispheres of radius 4 cm each. Find the number of such solid hemispheres.
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of solid sphere = 12 cm

Radius of small solid hemisphere = 4 cm 

Formula Used:

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3

Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3)πr3

Where, r = Radius of the sphere 

Calculation:

The volume of the small solid sphere with a radius of 12 cm = (4/3) × π × 123

The volume of the small solid sphere with a radius of 4 cm = (2/3) × π × 43

Number solid hemispheres. = (4/3) × π × 123/(2/3) × π × 43 = 2 × 27 = 54

∴ 54 of such hemispheres can be made.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 20 km/h, while the river is flowing at a speed of 8 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 6 h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (Vb) = 20 km/h

Speed of stream (Vs) = 8 km/h

Extra time upstream = 6 h

**Formula used:**

Speed downstream = Vb + Vs

Speed upstream = Vb - Vs

Time = Distance/Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = 20 + 8 = 28 km/h

Speed upstream = 20 - 8 = 12 km/h

Let distance be D, time downstream Td, and time upstream Tu. Tu = Td + 6

Distance same for both:

Downstream: D = 28 × Td

Upstream: D = 12 × (Td + 6)

⇒ 28 × Td = 12 × (Td + 6)

⇒ 28Td = 12Td + 72 16Td = 72 Td = 4.5

⇒ D = 28 × 4.5 = 126 km

**The distance is 126 km.**

 A = (√3/4) × a², where A is area and a is the side length.

questions.question: The average weight of 15 people increases by 3.2 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 52 kg. The weight of the new person is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

15 people, average increase = 3.2 kg, replaced person = 52 kg

**Formula:**

New average increase = old total + (new person - replaced person)

**Calculation:**

Total increase = 15 × 3.2 = 48 kg

New person = 52 kg + 48 kg = 100 kg

**The weight of the new person is 100 kg**

questions.question: Ramesh borrowed some money at rate of 5% per annum for the first four years, 8% per annum for the next six years, and 12% per annum for the period beyond ten years. If the total interest paid by him at the end of twelve years is ₹9,016, then find the money borrowed by Ramesh.
questions.solution:
Given:

Interest for first 4 years: 5% per annum

Interest for next 6 years: 8% per annum

Interest for period beyond 10 years (i.e., last 2 years): 12% per annum

Total interest paid after 12 years = ₹9,016

**Formula used:**

Interest (I) = (P × R × T) / 100 Where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.

**Calculation:**

⇒ For 4 years at 5% per annum: (I_1 = (P × 5 × 4) / 100 = (20P) / 100)

⇒ For 6 years at 8% per annum: (I_2 = (P × 8 × 6) / 100 = (48P) / 100)

⇒ For 2 years at 12% per annum: (I_3 = (P × 12 × 2) / 100 = (24P) / 100)

Total interest (I = I_1 + I_2 + I_3)

⇒ (9,016 = (20P + 48P + 24P) / 100)

⇒ (9,016 = (92P) / 100)

⇒ (P = 901,600 / 92) (P = 9,800)

**Ramesh borrowed ₹9,800.**

questions.question: The length and the breadth of the floor of a rectangular hall are 126 feet and 90 feet, respectively. What will be the area (in square feet) of each of the largest identical square tiles that can be used to tile this floor in a way that no part of the floor remains uncovered?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length = 126 feet

Breadth = 90 feet

**Calculation:**

To find the largest square tile size, We have to find the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of 126 and 90.

GCD(126, 90):

126 = 2 × 63 = 2 × 3 × 21 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7

90 = 2 × 45 = 2 × 3 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5

Common factors are 2 × 3 × 3 = 18.

So, the largest size of the square tile is 18 feet by 18 feet.

The area of each tile = 18 × 18 = 324 square feet.

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The price of a treadmill is marked at ₹1,250. A shopkeeper earns a profit of 14% after allowing a discount of 14% on the marked price. Find the cost price (to the nearest rupee) of the treadmill.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

MP (Marked Price) = ₹1250 Discount = 14% Profit = 14%

**Formula used:**

Discount Amount = MP × Discount%

Sale Price (SP) = MP - Discount Amount

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Discount Amount = 1250 × (14/100) = ₹175

SP = 1250 - 175 = ₹1075

CP = 1075 / (1 + (14/100)) = 1075 / 1.14 = ₹942.98 ≈ ₹943

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A person covers 28 km while walking at a speed of 8 km/h. How much distance (in km) will he cover in same time if he walks at a speed of 6 km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered = 28 km

Initial speed = 8 km/h

**Formula used:**

 Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

 The time taken to cover 28 km at 8 km/h

Time = 28 km / 8 km/h = 3.5 hours

New speed = 6 km/h

Distance covered at new speed = New speed × Time

= 6 km/h × 3.5 hours = 21 km

**He will cover 21 km at a speed of 6 km/h in the same time.**
